title: Large personal Atari ST, Amiga and DOS application/matching-game discovery
summary: Personally screen 563 candidate URLs and add 20 projects, with eight explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root assistant personally searched 16 GitHub query routes plus a primary README relationship, screened 563 unique URLs and reviewed 28 repositories. Adds 20 game/application/library recoveries and records eight non-promotions. All four requested platforms searched; no new CPC game-source candidate qualified in this pass. Strong application coverage includes Atari ST PrintMaster, Amiga AMOS, VEDIT DOS reconstruction and M602 screensaver. Historical compiler/runtime reuse, relocation-normalized matching, symbolic assembly versus C progress, behavior-derived reimplementations and source-preservation variants are explicit. No upstream compiler, game, installer, screensaver, firmware or downloaded binary executed. Build flags remain unverified rather than converting upstream assertions into independent checks.

sources.reason: Interpreter, tokenized program/bank loaders, editor and extension implementations derived from official AMOS source and binary research. This is language/application compatibility, not a game-specific CPU wrapper.
Disassembly-derived shape records, page geometry, text advance, borders and printer ABI support greeting-card, stationery and bitmap-editor pages; pm_render.py carries original addresses.
Mechanical translation of recovered SAVER.PAS preserves box motion, TP RNG, ordering and VGA text-buffer writes; BIOS/device boundaries are replaced by host services.
Recovered 1986 TETRIS.COM gameplay, shape/scoring records and text-mode hardware access, migrated from original TP3 to TP7.
Recovered game control flow, data and direct planar graphics/input routines in TP7, with no Crt/Graph/BGI dependency.
LE extraction/discovery, symbolic NASM round-trip and load-equivalent relinking with an incremental C replacement path for DOS CD 1.22h.
Recovered loader, chain file, overlays and structured game state. Verification explains TP3.02 compilation followed by fixed relocation/runtime normalization to the 1985 binaries.
Released source extended to recreate shareware/registered versions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2, retaining original game/support-library modules and version-specific data.
Terminal game reconstructed from SRE.EXE v0.994b, with structured empire/attack/economy modules and original-compatible data files; emulator comparisons are external tests.
Address-linked original campaign/procedure chain in C17 with low-level SDL3/host replacements. Inspected campaign driver is structured source, not a CPU register-dispatch loop.
Original Setup_Game/procedure chain reconstructed in C17, including rejection-sampled dice logic; separates original game logic from SDL3 platform boundaries.
Frozen semantically named C/assembly oracle with fresh one-link build accounting and explicit raw-debt inventory. Inspected keyboard module carries named hardware/IRQ semantics.
Modern map editor rebuilt from EdMap documentation, executable strings and WAD format specifications; actual egui command/state logic inspected.
Structured C reproduces original RNG, placement probing and line-count rules; separate Real48 implementation preserves TP scoring arithmetic rather than simply copying visible play.
Recovered full KING2 rules, RNG/deal ordering, contract selection and scoring implemented as structured native C with original procedure addresses.
Routine-addressed typed game state and actor logic reconstructed from AGA executable; external Unicorn/blitter harness checks original against TypeScript, not a CPU runtime in the game.
Historical editor source preserved; missing 8086-specific parts reconstructed via flattened 8080-to-8086 translation, plus binary/source-informed portable INSTALL/INTMOD replacements.

Repairs damaged small/compact libraries using surviving medium/large models, instruction/OMF transformation and recompiled C routines such as PRINTF. Surviving bytes and rebuilt modules are separately accounted.
Native C# simulation/game modules translated from neuromancer/wc1-re with DOS assets, Vulkan/SDL rendering and OPL2 audio model. Inspected fixed-point trig links to original function addresses.
Address-linked reconstructed C++ gameplay plus historical Borland build/equality gate, discovered via the related browser remake README.
Modern memory/debugging utility written in 2020, not a restoration of a historical application. Relevant general tooling is outside this focused discovery pass.

Source header explicitly says code, tables and structure are identical to the base Pole Chudes recovery and only string constants differ. Record the historical text variant without adding another engine entry.

Repository contains extensive decompiler output and a hybrid loader that maps original executable segments and detours only selected recompiled functions. Retain architectural/source-quality audit; whole-game native execution is not whole-game reconstructed-source execution.
Actual target is PlayStation SLUS_000.07, not DOS Alien Trilogy. Relevant source recovery, but outside the requested platform focus for this pass.

Runtime expressly retains guest register file, CFG/block dispatch, interpreter and real-mode memory model. Keep static-recompilation/game-specific emulation audit rather than present as high-level native EGA Trek recovery.
Early Windows Omikron engine reconstruction, not the older DOS game Nomad or an Amiga application. Primary README confirms Windows origin; outside this platform-focused pass.
Elm/browser remake is not established as source-derived by inspected README. Followed its explicit original-source link and promoted the separate zatacka-decomp matching project instead.

Useful visual/editorial research companion with decoded assets and room demonstrations, but playable original editions use emulators. Keep as a companion lead, not a new native game reconstruction; narrative seven-day paths explicitly are not a replay or full engine simulation.

decisions.title: AMOS Professional — TypeScript reimplementation
decisions.reason: Interpreter, tokenized program/bank loaders, editor and extension implementations derived from official AMOS source and binary research. This is language/application compatibility, not a game-specific CPU wrapper.

decisions.title: PrintMaster — Atari ST layout and browser reconstruction
decisions.reason: Disassembly-derived shape records, page geometry, text advance, borders and printer ABI support greeting-card, stationery and bitmap-editor pages; pm_render.py carries original addresses.

decisions.title: M602 screensaver — native C++ reconstruction port
decisions.reason: Mechanical translation of recovered SAVER.PAS preserves box motion, TP RNG, ordering and VGA text-buffer writes; BIOS/device boundaries are replaced by host services.

decisions.title: AcademySoft Tetris — Turbo Pascal recovery
decisions.reason: Recovered 1986 TETRIS.COM gameplay, shape/scoring records and text-mode hardware access, migrated from original TP3 to TP7.

decisions.title: Pole Chudes — DOS Turbo Pascal reconstruction
decisions.reason: Recovered game control flow, data and direct planar graphics/input routines in TP7, with no Crt/Graph/BGI dependency.

decisions.title: Warcraft: Orcs & Humans — symbolic DOS reconstruction
decisions.reason: LE extraction/discovery, symbolic NASM round-trip and load-equivalent relinking with an incremental C replacement path for DOS CD 1.22h.

decisions.title: Monopoly 1985 — Turbo Pascal matching source
decisions.reason: Recovered loader, chain file, overlays and structured game state. Verification explains TP3.02 compilation followed by fixed relocation/runtime normalization to the 1985 binaries.

decisions.title: Raptor — multi-version DOS source recreation
decisions.reason: Released source extended to recreate shareware/registered versions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2, retaining original game/support-library modules and version-specific data.

decisions.title: Solar Realms Elite — C++ BBS-game reconstruction
decisions.reason: Terminal game reconstructed from SRE.EXE v0.994b, with structured empire/attack/economy modules and original-compatible data files; emulator comparisons are external tests.

decisions.title: BattleTech: Crescent Hawks Revenge — C17 preservation port
decisions.reason: Address-linked original campaign/procedure chain in C17 with low-level SDL3/host replacements. Inspected campaign driver is structured source, not a CPU register-dispatch loop.

decisions.title: BattleTech: Crescent Hawks Inception — C17 preservation port
decisions.reason: Original Setup_Game/procedure chain reconstructed in C17, including rejection-sampled dice logic; separates original game logic from SDL3 platform boundaries.

decisions.title: Krypton Egg — historical matching DOS reconstruction
decisions.reason: Frozen semantically named C/assembly oracle with fresh one-link build accounting and explicit raw-debt inventory. Inspected keyboard module carries named hardware/IRQ semantics.

decisions.title: EdMap — Rust application reconstruction
decisions.reason: Modern map editor rebuilt from EdMap documentation, executable strings and WAD format specifications; actual egui command/state logic inspected.

decisions.title: Color Lines — native C engine reconstruction
decisions.reason: Structured C reproduces original RNG, placement probing and line-count rules; separate Real48 implementation preserves TP scoring arithmetic rather than simply copying visible play.

decisions.title: King — native C card-game reconstruction
decisions.reason: Recovered full KING2 rules, RNG/deal ordering, contract selection and scoring implemented as structured native C with original procedure addresses.

decisions.title: D/Generation — Amiga AGA TypeScript recovery
decisions.reason: Routine-addressed typed game state and actor logic reconstructed from AGA executable; external Unicorn/blitter harness checks original against TypeScript, not a CPU runtime in the game.

decisions.title: VEDIT — preserved editor and reconstructed DOS builds
decisions.reason: Historical editor source preserved; missing 8086-specific parts reconstructed via flattened 8080-to-8086 translation, plus binary/source-informed portable INSTALL/INTMOD replacements.

decisions.title: Watcom C 6.5 — damaged runtime-library restoration
decisions.reason: Repairs damaged small/compact libraries using surviving medium/large models, instruction/OMF transformation and recompiled C routines such as PRINTF. Surviving bytes and rebuilt modules are separately accounted.

decisions.reason: Modern memory/debugging utility written in 2020, not a restoration of a historical application. Relevant general tooling is outside this focused discovery pass.

decisions.title: Art1kDev/pole-chudes-mat
decisions.reason: Source header explicitly says code, tables and structure are identical to the base Pole Chudes recovery and only string constants differ. Record the historical text variant without adding another engine entry.

decisions.title: merlindk/dk-reconstructed
decisions.reason: Repository contains extensive decompiler output and a hybrid loader that maps original executable segments and detours only selected recompiled functions. Retain architectural/source-quality audit; whole-game native execution is not whole-game reconstructed-source execution.

decisions.title: lemiur/alien-trilogy-decomp
decisions.reason: Actual target is PlayStation SLUS_000.07, not DOS Alien Trilogy. Relevant source recovery, but outside the requested platform focus for this pass.

decisions.title: mabino/egatrek-port
decisions.reason: Runtime expressly retains guest register file, CFG/block dispatch, interpreter and real-mode memory model. Keep static-recompilation/game-specific emulation audit rather than present as high-level native EGA Trek recovery.

decisions.title: heyhippari/opennomad
decisions.reason: Early Windows Omikron engine reconstruction, not the older DOS game Nomad or an Amiga application. Primary README confirms Windows origin; outside this platform-focused pass.

decisions.title: SimonAlling/kurve
decisions.reason: Elm/browser remake is not established as source-derived by inspected README. Followed its explicit original-source link and promoted the separate zatacka-decomp matching project instead.

decisions.title: andresdelcampo/HomenajeLaAbadiaDelCrimen
